transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I’ve been having some trouble keeping track of things I really should be on top of. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I’ve missed or nearly missed heart follow-up appointments, forgot to call the clinic back, things like that. And sometimes I’ll go to do a repair job and realize I didn’t bring the right tools. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
Have you been experiencing these memory problems consistently over time?

Yeah… I’d say it’s been pretty steady for a while. Not my whole life or anything, at least not like this. It’s been causing real trouble for maybe a year and a couple months now. I think it started after that heart scare, when I had to cut back on the walking and little projects that used to sort of keep me settled. I don’t know if that makes sense, but that’s about when it became harder to ignore.
Have you been feeling anxious or depressed about these memory problems or any other issues?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say depressed, exactly. Anxious maybe a little, but mostly I just get frustrated or embarrassed when I realize I’ve dropped the ball on something. I try not to make a big deal of it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling sad or hopeless about your situation?

Not really hopeless, no. I mean, I have my moments where I feel discouraged or a little down on myself about it, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around feeling sad all the time. I hope that’s… the kind of answer you’re looking for.
Have you noticed any difficulties with learning new information?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think I’ve noticed a big problem learning new things… but I guess it depends what you mean by learning. If someone explains something to me clearly, I usually feel like I get it. I might need to hear it again, but I don’t know if that counts.
Do you have trouble recalling recent events or conversations?

I don’t think so, not in any major way. I mean, I might forget little bits of a conversation now and then, but I can usually remember the general idea. Recent events… I haven’t really noticed a big problem there. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
Have you noticed any changes in your personality or the way you typically behave?

I don’t think so… not anything major, anyway. I mean, I’m probably still pretty much myself. Maybe I get set in my ways sometimes, but I don’t know that I’d call that a personality change. If anything, people around me would probably notice before I would, right?
Do you have trouble with word-finding or expressing yourself when speaking?

Not really, no. I mean, once in a while I’ll be reaching for a word and it doesn’t come right away, but I figure that happens to everybody. I don’t think I have trouble expressing myself, at least not that I’ve noticed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any decline in your ability to perform daily tasks or make decisions?

Well… I’d like to say I’m doing alright day to day, and mostly I am, I think. But there have been a couple things. The repair group at the senior center, they used to count on me more, and lately I don’t think they can quite rely on me the same way. And my doctor’s office has had to call after me about missing some heart follow-ups. I don’t feel good about that. I’m not sure if that counts as a “decline,” but… it’s been happening.
Do you think your memory problems and trouble keeping track of things have significantly interfered with your daily life or relationships?

I guess… yes, probably more than I’d like to admit. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but the senior-center repair group, they can’t really count on me the way they used to, and that bothers me. And my doctor’s office has had to chase me a bit about missed heart follow-ups. So… I suppose it is interfering some, isn’t it?
Have you experienced any significant or traumatic events in your life, especially around the time your memory problems started?

Well… I wouldn’t want to call it traumatic exactly, because people go through worse, but I did have a cardiac scare a little over a year ago. After that I had to cut back on my walking and the little projects that used to keep me steady, I guess.

That’s about when things started causing real trouble — maybe a year and two months now. Does that sound like the kind of event you mean?
Do you think your ability to manage complex tasks has changed over the past year?

Yes… I think it has, though I don’t like saying it that way. The senior-center repair group used to be able to count on me more, and now I’ve dropped the ball enough that they don’t quite depend on me like before. And my doctor’s office has had to chase me about missed heart follow-ups, which is embarrassing.

So… I suppose with more complicated things, keeping all the pieces together has gotten harder over the past year. Is that the kind of change you mean?
Have you noticed any difficulty with planning or organizing tasks?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I don’t sit down and “plan” a lot of big things these days, so it’s a little hard for me to judge.

Sometimes I feel like I’m not as tidy about getting things in order as I used to be, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean by planning or organizing. I wouldn’t want to overstate it. Could you maybe give me an example of the kind of task you’re asking about?
Do you think your heart condition or any other medical issue has directly affected your memory or ability to keep track of things?

I don’t know if the heart condition itself is doing it directly… I wouldn’t want to say that if I’m not sure.

But what brings me in is that I keep forgetting things I really shouldn’t — like the heart follow-up appointments, or calling the clinic back when they ask me to. And even with the repair group, I’ll show up and realize I don’t have the right tools with me.

So maybe it’s connected somehow, or maybe it just made things more noticeable. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your ability to concentrate or pay attention over the past year?

Yes… somewhat. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I have noticed it.

Like, I’ll sit down at the bridge table, or at one of the Fix-It Friends planning meetings, really intending to pay attention. And for a little while I do. But then my mind sort of… slides off somewhere, and I come back to the conversation and realize I missed a good chunk of what was just said.

I don’t know if that counts as a significant change, but it’s been happening enough that I’ve noticed it.
Do you think your memory problems started after your heart condition was diagnosed or treated?

I’m not completely sure about the timing, to be honest. I don’t want to blame it on the heart issue if that’s not really fair.

What I can say is, since all that came up, it’s been more noticeable because I’m forgetting things that matter — like the heart follow-up appointments, or I’ll mean to call the clinic back and then it just slips. And with the repair jobs, I’ve shown up without the right tools, which is embarrassing.

So… maybe it started around then, or maybe that’s just when I started paying attention to it. Does that make sense?
Do you think your memory problems are more related to your heart condition or to stress, anxiety, or other emotional factors?

I’m not really sure, doctor. I mean, I suppose stress could make it worse, but I don’t know that I can honestly say it’s from stress or anxiety.

And I also don’t know that it’s the heart condition directly. I don’t want to point to the wrong thing and make more of it than I should.

What I can say is, I’ve noticed the forgetting and losing track of things more lately, but I’m not sure what’s causing it. Does that make sense?
Do you think your memory problems are more related to your physical health or to emotional factors like stress or anxiety?

I wish I could give you a clearer answer, but I really don’t know.

It could be my physical health, or it could be stress — I mean, I’m sure worrying about health doesn’t help anyone think clearly. But I haven’t noticed a clean pattern where I can say, “Oh, it’s definitely that.”

I just know I’ve been more aware of the memory trouble lately. I hope that’s an okay way to answer it.
Do you think your memory problems are more related to your physical health or emotional factors like stress, depression, or anxiety?

I’m sorry, I know I’m probably not giving you a very helpful answer, but I really can’t tell for sure.

I don’t want to say it’s physical health if it isn’t, and I don’t want to blame stress or anxiety either. I just haven’t noticed a clear pattern. It’s more that the memory trouble is there, and I’m not sure what it ties back to.

Is that okay? Or is there something more specific I should be looking for?
Have you experienced any decline in your motor skills or coordination over the past year?

I don’t think so, no. At least, I haven’t noticed anything major with coordination or motor skills.

I mean, I’m older, so I’m not as quick as I used to be, but I wouldn’t say there’s been a clear decline over the past year. If there’s something specific you mean by motor skills, I can try to think about it more.
